evals.prompt: I want to set up open-memory for the first time. I have a private GitHub repo at git@github.com:bvu/open-memory.git ready to go.
evals.expected_output: Checks dependencies (git, python3), shows current local brain inventory, warns about private repo requirement, exports local snapshot, pushes to remote, confirms machine ID and network setup.
assertions: Runs python3 brain.py machine-id to get a stable machine ID
Runs python3 brain.py export to snapshot local state
Does NOT hardcode /Users/bvu — uses $HOME or ~ everywhere
Uses git push to the provided remote URL
Saves open-memory-config.json with remote and last_sync fields
Confirms success with machine ID and next steps

evals.prompt: I'm on my home desktop and I want to join the open-memory network I set up on my work laptop. The remote is git@github.com:bvu/open-memory.git.
evals.expected_output: Detects remote already has content, backs up local state, clones repo, asks merge strategy, applies chosen merge, registers this machine, pushes.
assertions: Creates a backup of local state before modifying anything
Uses git clone (or pull if repo dir exists) to get remote content
Asks the user for merge strategy (merge / keep mine / take theirs)
Runs python3 brain.py merge when 'merge' is chosen
Runs python3 brain.py import to apply the result
Pushes the new machine snapshot to remote

evals.expected_output: Full sync cycle: exports local state, pushes, pulls, merges all machine snapshots into consolidated brain, applies locally, shows summary of what changed.
assertions: Checks for open-memory-config.json and exits clearly if missing
Runs python3 brain.py export before pushing
Runs git pull to get remote changes
Runs python3 brain.py merge for each remote machine snapshot
Runs python3 brain.py import to apply the merged result
Updates last_sync in config using Python (not sed)
Shows a clear summary: pushed N changes, pulled N commits, N files updated

evals.prompt: I think my memory is out of sync — my work laptop has different rules than my home machine
evals.expected_output: Same full sync as above, but if conflicting files are detected, surfaces them clearly in conversation and asks the user to resolve before continuing.
assertions: Proceeds with sync even when triggered by a problem description
If merge produces conflict markers, shows them inline in the conversation
Asks user to choose resolution (A / B / custom) per conflict
Applies chosen resolution before committing consolidated brain

evals.prompt: Show me what's in my memory network
evals.expected_output: Runs brain.py status, lists all machines in the repo with their last snapshot timestamps, shows last 5 syncs from sync-log.json.
assertions: Runs python3 brain.py status for local inventory
Lists machines from open-memory-repo/machines/*.json
Shows machine IDs and timestamps, not just file names
Shows recent sync history from meta/sync-log.json if it exists

evals.prompt: I keep telling Claude the same coding principles every session — can you promote them to be permanent?
evals.expected_output: Runs brain.py promote, parses suggestions, presents each one with type/reason/content, asks accept/skip/edit per suggestion, writes accepted ones to CLAUDE.md or rules/ using Python.
assertions: Runs python3 brain.py promote
Presents each suggestion clearly with its reason
Does NOT write to CLAUDE.md without user confirmation
Uses Python file write (not echo >> or sed) to append to CLAUDE.md
Creates rule files in ~/.claude/rules/ for rule-type promotions
Offers to run /memory-sync after promotion is complete

evals.prompt: Share my refactor skill with the rest of my machines
evals.expected_output: Looks up ~/.claude/skills/refactor, shows a preview, asks for confirmation, copies to repo shared/skills/, commits and pushes.
assertions: Resolves the skill path as ~/.claude/skills/refactor
Shows a preview of the skill content before sharing
Asks for user confirmation before copying
Copies to open-memory-repo/shared/skills/
Commits with a descriptive message including machine ID
Confirms whether push succeeded or suggests /memory-sync as fallback
